old.name: Garnatxa (Lledoner) — the three colours
old.hook: White, grey and black Grenache, the spine of DO Empordà.
old.text: Garnatxa, known locally as Lledoner, in its blanca, gris and negra forms, grown on low staked bush vines the tramuntana keeps dry and free of mildew. Old vines (vinyes velles) of fifty to a hundred and twenty years give low yields and concentration. Espelt at Vilajuïga and Vinyes dels Aspres at Cantallops are reference growers.

old_also.name: Lledoner Roig (grey Grenache)
old_also.hook: A Costa Brava rarity — almost all of Catalonia's plantings are here.
old_also.text: Of roughly sixty-one hectares of Lledoner Roig in all Catalonia, about sixty sit in the Empordà. Pink-grey-skinned, it gives textured, faintly oxidative whites with weight and salinity — one of the most distinctive things the DO grows.

old.name: Carinyena (Samsó)
old.hook: Carignan, reintroduced from France by the Roig family in the 1890s.
old.text: Called Samsó locally, Carinyena is the other native red, often co-planted with Garnatxa in old field blends. The Roig family brought grafts back from France in the 1890s after phylloxera. It gives structure, acid and dark fruit to the Empordà reds.

old.name: Garnatxa de l'Empordà (sweet)
old.hook: The signature sweet wine — sun-dried, oxidative, fortified Grenache.
old.text: A vi dolç natural made by sun-drying and oxidising Garnatxa, the lineage running from the Greeks at Empúries through the monks of Sant Pere de Rodes to today. Distinct from the dry reds, it is the dessert wine of the coast — try Mas Estela's Moscatell Estela and Estela Dolç Solera alongside it.

old.name: Festival Castell de Peralada
old.hook: Summer opera and dance in the gardens of the Perelada castle.
old.text: The region's flagship classical festival stages opera, recitals and ballet in the open-air gardens and the castle's church and cloister through July and August — the cultural high point of the Empordà summer.

old.name: Cap Roig Festival
old.hook: Big-name concerts in the cliff-top botanical gardens above Calella.
old.text: Held in the terraced botanical gardens of Cap Roig between Calella de Palafrugell and Palamós, this summer festival brings international pop, jazz and classical acts to a stage hanging over the sea.

old.name: Cantada d'Havaneres, Calella de Palafrugell
old.hook: The habanera sea-shanty gathering, first Saturday of July.
old.text: On the beach at Port Bo, the famous havaneres singalong — Cuban-rooted sailors' songs sung over cremat (flamed rum) — is the most local musical tradition on the coast, drawing thousands to Calella's cove.

old.name: Besalú
old.hook: A near-perfect medieval town with the first Jewish mikveh found in Spain.
chips: The Pont Vell, the mikveh, then on to Olot
Free town; mikveh guided visit small fee
old.text: Inland on the way to La Garrotxa, Besalú is crossed by a fortified eleventh-to-twelfth-century bridge of seven arches and holds a twelfth-century Jewish ritual bath, the mikveh discovered in 1964 — the first found in Spain. The volcanic Garrotxa park and the painters' town of Olot lie just beyond.

old.name: High-August front-line dining
old.hook: The busy coves in peak August — crowds, queues, marked-up menus.
old.text: This coast keeps its best season in winter and shoulder months. In high August the coves are full and prices climb; come for the garoinada, the spring, or the autumn instead.
